about.title: Larkspur Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Larkspur is a small city, but its traffic doesn't stay small during Friday rush hour, when reported crashes tend to cluster between 4 and 6 p.m. on corridors like Magnolia Avenue, Esfd Boulevard, and the US-101 corridor. Marin County's most recent full-year data counted 39 injury collisions here, with 54 people hurt. Behind each number is someone dealing with medical appointments, missed work, and an insurance adjuster looking for a quick, low-value resolution. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your case directly — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney who takes Larkspur car accident cases on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless money is recovered on your behalf. The sooner evidence is gathered after a crash, the stronger a claim tends to be, so reaching out early matters.

whyChoose.title: What Matters After a Larkspur Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity, like the county or a public transit agency, is involved. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a Larkspur crash, you can still recover a reduced share of damages. Insurers know this and often try to shift blame onto you early, sometimes during a recorded statement.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in most car accident cases. That makes it especially important not to accept a fast settlement offer before the full extent of your injuries is understood.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize or deny your claim, and even a casual comment about feeling 'fine' can be used against you later. An independent attorney can communicate with the insurer on your behalf.

items.question: What if my accident happened on US-101 or another state highway near Larkspur?
How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Larkspur?
items.answer: Under California law, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your claim involves a government-owned road or vehicle, though, a much shorter deadline — sometimes just six months — may apply, so it's worth getting an evaluation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and attorneys in our network handle car accident cases on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after your initial conversation.
